items.statement: A UN General Assembly resolution on the war in Ukraine exists: on 24 February 2026 the General Assembly adopted a resolution calling for an 'immediate, full and unconditional ceasefire' between Russia and Ukraine and for a 'comprehensive, just and lasting peace' based on international law. The vote was 107 in favour, 12 against and 51 abstentions (BTA, citing DPA). This is the document that makes Iotova's blanket statement 'there is no UN General Assembly resolution' false if it is read literally; the resolution is political and non-binding, so Gyurov's 'the resolution envisaged a cessation of hostilities' is loose but substantially accurate.
items.quote: Общото събрание на ООН в Ню Йорк призова снощи чрез резолюция за незабавно прекратяване на огъня и траен мир в Украйна, в деня на четвъртата годишнина от пълномащабната инвазия на Русия в страната, предаде ДПА. Общо 107 държави членки на световната организация гласуваха в подкрепа на резолюцията в Ню Йорк, 12 гласуваха против, а 51 се въздържаха. Резолюцията призовава за „незабавно, пълно и безусловно прекратяване на огъня“ между Русия и Украйна и изисква „всеобхватен, справедлив и траен мир“ на основата на международното право.
items.source: БТА — „Общото събрание на ООН призова за прекратяване на огъня и мир в Украйна“ (по ДПА)

items.statement: Bulgaria was among the EU member states that voted in favour of the 24 February 2026 UN General Assembly resolution. Nedeljnik's vote report lists Bulgaria alongside Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Poland, Romania, Croatia and Slovenia as EU members that voted for the text, while Serbia and the United States abstained. This is the best available direct statement of Bulgaria's position on that resolution; no Bulgarian official roll-call or MFA statement listing the vote was found.
items.quote: Srbija se našla upravo u toj grupi uzdržanih zemalja, među kojima su još i Sjedinjene Američke Države. Takva odluka razlikuje se od stava većine članica EU, uključujući Nemačku, Francusku, Italiju, Španiju, Poljsku, Rumuniju, Bugarsku, Hrvatsku i Sloveniju, koje su glasale za rezoluciju.
items.source: Nedeljnik — „Rezolucija o miru u Ukrajini usvojena u UN: Srbija uzdržana, dok su članice EU glasale 'za'“

items.statement: The document at the centre of the September 2026 row was a joint declaration/statement on Ukraine, not a UN General Assembly resolution. More than 50 states signed it ahead of the UN Security Council meeting on Ukraine; Bulgaria was among the 51 signatories, and all 27 EU member states signed. It called on Russia to agree to a full, immediate and unconditional ceasefire and to begin substantive peace negotiations. This is the 'statement' Iotova distinguished from a 'resolution' in the debate.
items.quote: More than 50 countries signed the document ahead of the UN Security Council's meeting on Ukraine. The declaration calls on Russia to agree to a full, immediate, and unconditional ceasefire in Ukraine and to begin substantive peace negotiations. ... According to a list published on the website of Ukraine's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Bulgaria is among the 51 countries that signed the declaration. A check by BTA revealed that the statement was signed by all 27 EU Member States.
items.source: БНР (Radio Bulgaria in English) — „Bulgaria joins UN declaration on Ukraine“

items.statement: Iotova said she did not sign the September 2026 statement and did not attend the expanded UN Security Council meeting; she said the text was sent to all UN member states before the session and that Bulgaria 'had no opportunity to express reservations' or have amendments accepted. The Foreign Ministry, by contrast, said Bulgaria had endorsed the declaration to support European unity, while conceding that Bulgaria's national position was not fully reflected in it. This is a documented split between the President and the Foreign Ministry over the same document, and it explains why the debate exchange slides between 'resolution' and 'statement'.
items.quote: In a Facebook post published on Friday, President Iliana Iotova addressed media reports that she had signed a joint statement on Ukraine following an expanded UN Security Council meeting on the issue on Wednesday. Iotova reported that she did not sign the statement. The president wrote: "[The statement] was sent to all UN Member States before the session in New York. Bulgaria had no opportunity to express reservations about the position presented, nor were the proposed amendments accepted. For this reason, I did not attend the expanded meeting of the Council, as evidenced by my absence from the group photo afterwards."
items.source: БТА — „President Addresses Reports of Bulgaria Signing UN Statement on Ukraine“

items.statement: Iotova did address the UN General Assembly: on 23 September 2026 she spoke in the general debate of the 81st session, delivering a speech centred on Black Sea security and calling for the Black Sea to be turned from a high-risk zone into a zone of national and international security. The Presidential website records the speech and the 81st session; this part of her debate claim is documented. The separate question is the '193 states' formulation (see next item).
items.quote: България призовава: да превърнем Черно море от зона на повишен риск и заплаха в зона на национална и международна сигурност – зона на безопасност, зона на свободни транспортни, енергийни, търговски, дигитални коридори, на туризъм, зона, където се срещат в мир различни култури, религии и политически системи. Това заяви държавният глава Илияна Йотова в изказването си на 81-вата сесия на Общото събрание на ООН.
items.source: Президент на Република България — „Държавният глава пред ООН: От зона на повишен риск да превърнем Черно море в зона на национална и международна сигурност“

items.statement: The UN General Assembly is composed of all 193 UN member states, each with one vote; its annual general debate is the forum in which member states express their views. The figure '193 states' in Iotova's debate statement therefore matches the Assembly's membership, not a verified count of heads of state or government present in the hall. The general debate is addressed by states, often through ministers, and attendance varies by day, so 'before leaders of 193 states' is a rhetorical formulation rather than a documented attendance figure.
items.quote: Each of the 193 Member States in the Assembly has one vote.
items.source: United Nations — General Assembly, Functions and powers of the General Assembly

items.statement: Iotova convened the Consultative Council on National Security (КСНС) on 7 October 2026 — the first КСНС of her term as head of state — the day after two foreign-flagged merchant ships were hit by sea and air drones in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea. The stated topic was 'Current risks and threats to maritime security and the critical infrastructure of Bulgaria in the context of the war in Ukraine'. This fixes the date and the trigger of the session that both candidates discussed.
items.quote: Президентът Илияна Йотова свика за днес първия в мандата си като държавен глава и върховен главнокомандващ Консултативен съвет за национална сигурност. Заседанието ще се проведе само ден след като два търговски кораба, плаващи под чужд флаг, бяха поразени от бойни морски и въздушни дронове, в периметъра на изключителната икономическа зона на България в Черно море. Темата на разискванията е: "Актуални рискове и заплахи за морската сигурност и критичната инфраструктура на България в контекста на войната в Украйна“.
items.source: БНР — „Президентът Йотова свиква КСНС заради поразените от дронове кораби“

items.statement: The 7 October 2026 КСНС did produce a published opinion and concrete proposals, not merely a discussion: it condemned the strikes on merchant ships in the Black Sea as a gross violation of international maritime law, demanded an investigation and public reporting of the perpetrator, called for an immediate ceasefire and active Bulgarian participation in the peace process, and listed measures including anti-drone systems, NATO/EU monitoring and a UN resolution on freedom and safety of navigation in the Black Sea. This is relevant to Gyurov's debate criticism that the council met 'too late, without concrete decisions and without concrete goals'; the lateness is a judgment, but the 'no concrete decisions' part is not supported by the published opinion.
items.quote: Консултативният съвет за национална сигурност категорично осъжда ударите по търговските кораби в Черно море като грубо нарушение на международното морско право и настоява за незабавно извършване на проверка за установяване на извършителя на ударите. След приключване на проверката изпълнителната власт да уведоми обществеността за резултатите. Най-големите гаранции за нашата сигурност е незабавно прекратяване на огъня и използването на всички политически и дипломатически канали за постигане на мир. България трябва да участва активно в този процес.
items.source: Президент на Република България — „ЗАСЕДАНИЕ НА КСНС НА 07.10.2026 г.“, Становище и предложения

items.statement: Bulgaria did impose a veto on North Macedonia's EU accession process in 2020, and it lifted it on 24 June 2022 by adopting the French EU Council Presidency's proposal. BNT reports that the National Assembly voted 170 in favour of giving the government a mandate to accept the French proposal and that this 'lifts the veto imposed by Bulgaria in 2020'. The decision was conditional on the 2017 friendship treaty, Bulgarians being written into North Macedonia's constitution on an equal footing with other peoples, no recognition of a 'Macedonian language', and European guarantees. This directly contradicts Iotova's debate statement that she does not remember Bulgaria ever imposing a veto.
items.quote: Със 170 гласа "за" парламентът прие предложението на "Демократична България" за предоставяне на мандат на Министерски съвет да приеме предложението на Френското председателство за Северна Македония. НС на практика дава мандат на МС да приеме т.н. френско предложение за започване на преговори на Северна Македония с ЕС и вдига ветото, наложено от България през 2020 г.
items.source: БНТ Новини — „Парламентът свали ветото за Северна Македония – вижте при какви условия“

items.statement: The official text of the 47th National Assembly's decision confirms the conditions attached to the French proposal. The decision (State Gazette No. 48 of 28 June 2022, adopted 24 June 2022) authorises the government to approve the draft negotiating framework and Council conclusions proposed by the then EU Council Presidency only if the text guarantees that Bulgarians are written into North Macedonia's constitution in the provisions mentioning other peoples and on an equal footing, that nothing in the accession process can be read as Bulgarian recognition of a 'Macedonian language', that good-neighbourliness remains a horizontal criterion, and that the 2017 treaty and joint committee protocols are referenced. This is the primary legal text behind the 'French proposal' vote.
items.quote: Решение на Четиридесет и седмото Народно събрание на Република България във връзка с разширяването на Европейския съюз и процеса на преговори на Република Северна Македония ... Решението е прието от 47-ото народно събрание на 24 юни 2022 г. и е подпечатано с официалния печат на Народното събрание.
items.source: Държавен вестник, бр. 48 от 28.06.2022 г. — Решение на 47-ото Народно събрание във връзка с разширяването на ЕС и процеса на преговори на Република Северна Македония

items.statement: The EU opened accession negotiations with North Macedonia and Albania at intergovernmental conferences in Brussels on 19 July 2022, implementing the European Council's March 2020 decision. This is the outcome that followed the Bulgarian parliament's 24 June 2022 decision to accept the French Presidency proposal; the holding of the intergovernmental conferences confirms that the block had been overcome in fact, not only in Bulgarian domestic wording.
items.quote: Today, we have finally taken important steps forward in the opening of accession negotiations with North Macedonia and Albania. Intergovernmental Conferences at ministerial level were held in Brussels to implement the decision by the European Council of March 2020 to open accession talks.
items.source: Council of the European Union — Statement by President Charles Michel on the occasion of Intergovernmental Conferences on the accession with North Macedonia and with Albania

items.statement: Finland and Norway did hold direct contact with Putin, but the official record describes a phone call to convey messages, not negotiations. On 27 October 2026 Finland's President Alexander Stubb and Norway's Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre called Putin in Helsinki, a follow-up to the Oslo meeting of 20 October and held in consultation with Ukraine. The stated aim was 'to convey messages directly regarding future negotiations', and the two leaders acted for their own countries, not for Europe as a whole. Iotova's debate statement that 'for two days countries like Finland and Norway started negotiating with President Putin' is therefore an overstatement of a real call: the call happened two days before the debate, and Stubb did open direct dialogue, but the official description is message-conveying, not negotiation.
items.quote: President of the Republic of Finland Alexander Stubb and Prime Minister of Norway Jonas Gahr Støre made a phone call with President of Russia Vladimir Putin on Tuesday 27 October in Helsinki. The call was a follow-up of the meeting in Oslo on 20 October and held in consultation with Ukraine. Stubb and Støre initiated the call to discuss Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine and the diplomatic efforts to end the war and promote peace and stability in Europe. ... The aim of the call was to convey messages directly regarding future negotiations to help to end the war to President Putin. ... Stubb and Støre took the call as leaders of their respective countries and did not speak on the behalf of Europe as a whole.
items.source: Office of the President of the Republic of Finland — Press release 66/2026, „President Stubb and Prime Minister Støre held a phone call with President Putin“

open_questions: The UN press release for the 24 February 2026 resolution (press.un.org/en/2026/ga12752.doc.htm) returned HTTP 404, and the UNGA voting record (A/ES-11/PV.23) could not be retrieved; the 107-12-51 count is triangulated from BTA (citing DPA), Xinhua and Ukrinform, but the individual roll-call was not obtained.

No Bulgarian official document or UN roll-call explicitly listing Bulgaria's vote on the 24 February 2026 resolution was found. Bulgaria's 'yes' rests on Nedeljnik's list of EU member states voting in favour; a Bulgarian MFA statement or the UN voting record would settle it.

The claim that Iotova spoke 'before leaders of 193 states' is only partly verifiable: she addressed the 81st UNGA general debate on 23 September 2026, and the UNGA has 193 member states, but no attendance list shows 193 heads of state or government present, and the general debate includes ministers and varies by day.

Iotova's statement 'there is no UN General Assembly resolution' is literally contradicted by the 24 February 2026 resolution, but the exchange may have been about the September 2026 declaration, which was not a resolution. The transcript does not resolve which document she meant; the record contains both a resolution and a declaration.

Whether the 2020 Bulgarian block was a formal 'veto' is a matter of nomenclature: enlargement decisions require unanimity and Bulgaria refused to approve the negotiating framework, which functioned as a veto and was reported as one, but no formal vote labelled 'veto' was found. The exact date of the refusal (6 November 2020) comes from a separate BNT report, not from the 2022 article used in the evidence.

The full text of the French Presidency's June 2022 proposal was not obtained. The State Gazette decision and BNT reporting describe its content and conditions, and the Council statement confirms the 19 July 2022 intergovernmental conferences, but the proposal itself was not retrieved.

The KСНС declaration's adoption is reported by BNR as a three-quarters majority with three parliamentary groups against; the president.bg page publishes the opinion but not the vote, so the exact majority is single-sourced.

Finland and Norway did hold a call with Putin on 27 October 2026, but neither the Finnish release nor the Kremlin readout describes them as negotiating a settlement; Iotova's 'started negotiating' is an overstatement. The content of the Abu Dhabi talks and whether Finland or Norway will participate in them is outside this cluster.

Several pages could not be used: OFFNews and the live Consilium page returned HTTP 403/blocked, the BTA and BNR article bodies were partly truncated by navigation, and the UN document viewer returned only a shell; these were replaced by archives or other sources where possible.

No archive.org snapshot was found for the State Gazette decision page (dv.parliament.bg, idMat=174371); the two president.bg pages were archived during this research on 31 October 2026, so those snapshots are same-day captures, not contemporaneous ones.
notes: The cluster is strong on the core chronology and cuts both ways. The UN General Assembly did adopt a resolution on the war on 24 February 2026 (107-12-51) calling for an immediate, full and unconditional ceasefire, and Bulgaria is listed among the EU states voting for it; that makes Iotova's blanket 'there is no UNGA resolution' false as stated, and gives real support to Gyurov's 'the resolution envisaged a cessation of hostilities', though the text is non-binding and 'envisaged' is loose. Iotova is nonetheless right that the September 2026 document was a declaration, not a resolution, and the President/Foreign Ministry split over whether Bulgaria signed it is documented. Her UNGA speech on 23 September 2026 is documented; the '193 states' figure is the Assembly's membership, not a verified count of leaders present. The КСНС was convened on 7 October 2026, the day after the Black Sea ship strikes, and produced a detailed published opinion with concrete proposals, so Gyurov's 'too late, no concrete decisions' is only partly fair: the timing is a judgment, the 'no concrete decisions' part is not supported. On North Macedonia, the 2020 veto and its 24 June 2022 lifting through the French Presidency proposal are documented in BNT's report (170 votes in favour, and the explicit statement that the decision lifts the veto imposed in 2020) and in the State Gazette decision (which records the conditions), and the EU opened talks on 19 July 2022; Iotova's 'I don't remember a veto' is contradicted. On Finland and Norway, the 27 October 2026 call is real and Stubb did open direct dialogue, but the official description is message-conveying in consultation with Ukraine, not negotiation on behalf of Europe. The weakest links are the absence of the UN roll-call and of a Bulgarian official statement on the 24 February vote, and the fact that the September declaration's exact legal status rests on the President's and Foreign Ministry's competing characterisations.
